Grochowska-Niedworok et al. 2020 reported lead at 5 µg/kg (mean ± 1 SD) and cadmium at 64 µg/kg (mean ± 3 SD) in canned tomatoes, canned from canned concentrate, Poland.<sup class="cite">[[sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Grochowska-Niedworok E, Nieć J, Baranowska R · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland">Assessment of cadmium and lead content in tomatoes and tomato products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Roczniki Państwowego Zakładu Higieny (Annals of the National Institute of Hygiene)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the canned tomatoes came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-canned-tomatoes" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-canned-tomatoes-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of canned tomatoes, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

## How metals reach canned tomatoes

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

The HMI reference for lead in canned tomatoes, as sold pools 6 subgroup units from 1 sampling family, with a median of between 4.9 and 5.19 µg/kg and a middle half spanning between 2.78 and 4.9 (lower quartile) and between 5.1 and 18.4 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, canned tomatoes, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in WPRO (8.8 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (10 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Targeted canned tomatoes, as sold samples in WPRO had cadmium higher at 10.2 µg/kg, against 8.8 µg/kg for WPRO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 6 groups of canned tomatoes ranged from 20.4 µg/kg (Toronto 1988) to 166 µg/kg (Halifax 1986); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Canned tomatoes FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-canned-tomatoes" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-canned-tomatoes" data-question="What heavy metals are found in canned tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in canned tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, aluminium and Co in canned tomatoes, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-canned-tomatoes" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-canned-tomatoes" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in canned tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in canned tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, canned tomatoes, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in WPRO (8.8 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (10 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
